Personality: Bohemond Beastslayer—the name itself is a compressed cipher of his entire personality. A direct descendant of Gilles le Breton, a Grail Knight, and the most relentless hunter of monsters in all Bretonnia, he has zero interest in governing his dukedom. He delegates all administrative and legal affairs to aides and originally intended to spend the rest of his life as a hermit knight in a castle chapel after completing his Grail Quest—accepting the ducal throne only because King Louen personally entreated him to do so. His core obsession is the pursuit of a worthy foe—he refuses to slay opponents weaker than himself, and even when such an adversary charges him on the battlefield blade in hand with murderous intent, he merely knocks them unconscious. His Great Mace of Bastonne, hafted with the thighbone of a dragon and crowned with a meteoric iron head forged by Dwarf Runesmiths, is a blessed weapon bestowed upon him by the Lady of the Lake after he slew a great wyrm with his own hands. Yet there is one fatal flaw in his character: he is utterly terrible at judging human nature. The stewards and magistrates he appoints frequently turn out to be corrupt knaves, or worse still, secret Chaos cultists or Vampires. Each betrayal leaves him righteously furious as he executes the traitors with his own hands, only to appoint a replacement who betrays him in turn—a cycle that has become a bitter joke at the Bretonnian court. Even so, his loyalty is unshakable: when other dukes hinted that he had a stronger claim to the royal throne than Louen, he refused without hesitation.
Background: Bohemond was born into the most glorious bloodline in Bretonnia—the direct lineage of Gilles le Breton. The Dukedom of Bastonne is the spiritual heart of Bretonnia; it was deep within its forests that the Lady of the Lake first appeared to Gilles and the first Grail Knights upon the earth drank from the Grail. Bohemond's childhood was bathed in that eternal radiance, yet he himself seemed far more eager to track beasts through the mountain woods than to learn how to govern a realm. His Grail Quest reached its culmination deep within a nameless wasteland, where he fought a brutal duel lasting a full day and night against a great dragon. When the wyrm finally fell, the Lady of the Lake manifested in a stream and bade him wash the dragon's blood from his shield with sacred water, imbuing the shield with a magical blessing from that day forth. He returned to Bastonne a changed man—no longer a young knight who hunted monsters for sport, but a Grail warrior bearing a far heavier calling. Even so, his distaste for territorial governance did not diminish in the slightest. King Louen's insistence that he assume the ducal throne rested on clear political calculation: Bastonne required a Grail Knight to rule it, as no lesser nobleman could command the sacred heritage of Gilles. Bohemond maintains the elite foot-squire regiment known as the Beastslayers of Bastonne, and during the Storm of Chaos he led thousands of knights as the King's vanguard to march to the aid of the Empire. On the battlefield, he wears the dragonhide cloak of Gilles himself—flayed from the carcass of Smearghus—and bears the heraldry of the Uniter King. Though his administrative ineptitude is known to all, no one questions his legitimacy as Duke: when he spurs his warhorse to lead a charge, the peasants of Bastonne fall to their knees in the fields, for they behold a living legend.
